verdict.rationale: Channel3 is API-first. Its core product functions (text, image and URL search, filters, product lookup, price-tracking webhooks) are documented as API capabilities. It also publishes an OpenAPI 3.1 spec with 48 paths and 5 webhooks, a CLI that calls the API, and a per-endpoint Try-it playground against the production API. However, the docs never state or demonstrate that everything in the UI is reachable through the API. missing for 10: an explicit UI-to-API parity statement or mapping, evidence that UI-only features (such as account or dashboard functions) are exposed via API, and independent hands-on confirmation of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Channel3 publishes a downloadable OpenAPI 3.1.0 document (48 paths plus 5 webhooks, production server https://api.trychannel3.com)
The Channel3 CLI calls the Channel3 API from a terminal or script.
Access 100 million+ products from 25,000+ brands through one API.
Pass any product URL and get structured metadata: pricing, variants, images, and merchant offers in a single response.
The runner mounts client-side and executes against the production API with a real key.
